verdict: Higher prices did the work: sales rose just 3% as shoppers bought less, but easing cocoa-era costs and tariff refunds more than doubled Hershey's profit.

segments.name: North America Confectionery
segments.note: Chocolate and candy in the US and Canada — about 13 points of price increases offset an 11-point drop in volume.

segments.name: North America Salty Snacks
segments.note: Pretzels, popcorn and salty snacks; the LesserEvil acquisition contributed about 20 points of the growth.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Sales outside North America, which fell as volume dropped.

opex.name: Selling, marketing & administrative
opex.note: Selling, marketing and administrative spending — advertising and consumer marketing rose 17% in the quarter.

opex.name: Business realignment costs
opex.note: Costs of Hershey's business realignment program — just $0.5M this quarter.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $48.7M plus $1.0M of other expense, taken out of profit.

takeaways.title: Price up, volume down
takeaways.text: Price increases added about 11 points to sales growth while volume and mix subtracted about 10 — shoppers paid more and bought less, and pricing won.

takeaways.title: Margins snapped back
takeaways.text: Reported gross margin jumped from 32.6% to 46.1% on price realization, lower net commodity costs, productivity savings, tariff refunds and derivative gains; even the adjusted margin rose to 42.7%.

takeaways.title: The core candy business earned it
takeaways.text: North America Confectionery segment income rose 66% to $950M — a 35.8% segment margin — carrying the quarter while International segment results stayed in loss.

oneTimers: Reported gross profit includes $113M of unallocated mark-to-market gains on commodity derivatives — a paper gain that is why reported gross margin (46.1%) sits above the adjusted figure (42.7%).
Tariff refunds added $0.22 to adjusted EPS in the quarter.
Unallocated corporate costs include $36M of acquisition and integration spending, mainly for LesserEvil and Sour Strips.
follow100Note: Hershey reports to the nearest thousand in its 10-Q; the chart rounds those figures to the nearest $0.5M (net sales $3,275.5M, net income $580.8M before rounding).
